name: Hangaza
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Simon, Chipanda. 2023. Verbal affix ordering in Hangaza language. Journal of Linguistics, Literary and Communication Studies 2(1): 41-54. doi:10.58721/jltcs.v2i1.304
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Morphology paper; no phonology section. p. 48: 'the past tense has been toned; hence in some contexts, prosody contributes to affix ordering'; p. 50 generic remark that 'tone, stress, and intonation.. may trigger allomorphs ordering', example 12(a) 'influenced by high tone'. No statement of where stress falls or whether Hangaza has stress.

sources.citation: Simon, Chipanda. 2024. Portmanteau manifestations of -j- and -k- morphs of verb extension in Hangaza. African Journal of Social Issues 6(1): 127-143. doi:10.4314/ajosi.v6i1.9
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 127 and p. 141: recommends that 'other studies can be done on the Hangaza prosodic features' -- the author treats prosody as undescribed.

sources.citation: Muzale, Henry R. T. & Josephat M. Rugemalira. 2008. Researching and documenting the languages of Tanzania. Language Documentation & Conservation 2(1): 68-108.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: LOT project overview, not a description. pp. 74-75: 'In Kihangaza, Ruhaya, Ciruuri, and Runyambo, vowel length is distinctive, with five short and five long vowels'; tone marking in the LOT lexicons is partial; p. 75: unpublished 'grammar notes exist for.. Kihangaza'. Lists Rubagumya 2006 Igihangaza Lexicon (LOT Lexicon Series 4). No stress statement.
Segment inventory includes MODIFIER LETTER HIGH TONE BAR and LOW TONE BAR (two tones). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page hang1260 and reference search (Hangaza / Igihangaza / Rubagumya / Jouannet)
sources.note: Only 2 descriptive references (the two 2010 UDSM MA theses); title search adds Rubagumya 2006 lexicon (3 records) and Tracey 1950 (music recordings). No phonology or grammar of Hangaza is on record.

sources.citation: Languages of Tanzania (LOT) Project. n.d. Kihangaza grammar notes (unpublished; reported in Muzale & Rugemalira 2008: 75).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Muzale & Rugemalira 2008 report that LOT grammar notes exist for Kihangaza (with Kimashami and Cigogo); the Runyambo grammar built on the same template has a phonology chapter.
